On the left the roots pair the two centers (outlined in accent) and the cheapest edit path costs 0. On the right the roots force leaf 2 of the first star onto the center of the second, and the cheapest path costs 8: four edges deleted and four inserted to rewire the star around its new center." width="100%"} This is the general interface behind `graph_edit_distance(exact=True)`, `optimal_edit_paths()` and `optimize_graph_edit_distance()`. The search yields each complete edit path it accepts: with `strictly_decreasing=True` (default) each path is cheaper than the one before, so the last is optimal; with `strictly_decreasing=False` it also yields paths that tie the best cost so far, so the trailing run of equal costs lists every optimal path. Use it when you need both the paths and control over the search, such as forcing two root nodes to correspond with `roots=` or capping the running time with `timeout=`. The whole search runs before the first path is yielded, so breaking out early saves no time. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The target graph. When it runs out, the paths found so far are yielded. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Iterator[tuple]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Triples `(node_path, edge_path, cost)`, in the format of `optimal_edit_paths()`, with `cost` a `float`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs differ in directedness, a cost is negative or not a number, a root is not in its graph, or `timeout=` is not positive. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~optimal_edit_paths`) : Every cheapest edit path. [](`~graph_edit_distance`) : The edit distance alone. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Mirrors NetworkX's `optimize_edit_paths()`, with edge IDs in the edge paths in place of endpoint tuples. Which intermediate paths are found depends on the order in which equally good assignments are explored, so they can differ from NetworkX's; the final cost does not. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star compared with itself is at distance `0` when the centers are forced to correspond, but forcing a leaf to correspond to the center costs `8`: the edit path has to rewire the star around a new center. In this six-node star, node `1` is the center and node `2` a leaf: ::: {#1a8da864 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(6) [cost for _, _, cost in star.optimize_edit_paths(star, roots=(1, 1))][-1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#808b578a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [cost for _, _, cost in star.optimize_edit_paths(star, roots=(2, 1))][-1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 8.0 ``` ::: :::
